It reflects what a school could serve based on the total number of classrooms in a standard program offering.

It's a more fixed number, it's more static, with the exception of if you have a classroom addition or if we have a major renovation of the building. We transitioned to base capacity a number of years ago, in part when we were doing attendance zone change processes like now, where we would have an overwhelming number of parents coming advocating for their children, as they

Part of our partnership with LCPS, and we are here to educate all children, all

children deserve to be educated at the school closest to their school. We started calculating base capacity, that given the prototype size of a school. So as an example, we have a 34-classroom school. We assessed that we should have at least five classrooms available for special programs or special education so that siblings can go to school together if in fact one is a special education student. So we started calculating base capacity that way.

We also calculated base capacity in part when we were still half-day kindergarten. And so you could potentially have seven kindergarten classes, which would be four classrooms, but then the next year it might just be six half days, and so that's three classrooms. And so capacities were changing every year, and it was really hard for parents to understand, "Well, why has my capacity changed this year?" So

we transitioned to the base building capacity because it addressed our special program needs. That also was endorsed by policy, where we cannot rezone, we cannot change special education classrooms just because of the boundary, and because it gave a more consistent look at a building. I wouldn't say ideal, but it identified where we had space. Program capacity, on the other hand, reflects what's actually happening in the

school. So we were talking about the STEP classes that are at Rolling Ridge or the STEP classroom at Meadowland. STEP has a maximum enrollment of 16 students per class. Base capacity, we're calculating it at 23 because that's what our typical school is. At a Head Start or at a Title I school, it's reduced to 20. But program is what's actually serving. So it's more dynamic.

It reflects what's happening that school year and can change depending on the programs that are in that school. Program capacity is also almost always lower number than base capacity.
